question.problem: The $12$ members of a student council are asked to elect among themselves a leadership team: a president, a vice-president, and a secretary. How many different leadership teams are possible?
question.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $12$ members to choose from, so $n=12.$ We want to select $3$ of those members to be in the leadership team, so we have $r=3.$

Therefore, the number of different $3$-member leadership teams is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{12}{P}_{3} & =\frac{12!}{(12-3)!} \\  & =\frac{12!}{9!} \\  & =\frac{12\cdot 11\cdot 10\cdot \cancel{9!}}{\cancel{9!}} \\  & =12\cdot 11\cdot 10 \\  & =1\,320.\end{aligned}
$$
